title: Online shop on one cloud account

organisation.name: Halden Outdoor
organisation.summary: Halden Outdoor sells camping gear online. Customers browse and pay through the shop web app behind a CDN; card payments go to an external payment provider, which reports results back to the orders API by webhook. The orders database keeps order history, addresses and payment tokens, and a nightly job writes order exports to a storage bucket that finance downloads. Two platform engineers run everything in one cloud account and deploy from a hosted CI pipeline with a long-lived access key.

cloud_security.summary: The CI deploy key leaks and is used from outside to read the order exports
A bucket policy change makes the exports bucket readable from the internet

identity_access.summary: Password spraying against staff admin accounts that have no MFA
The never-rotated deploy-prod user is the identity an attacker uses to change the account

application_security.summary: Stored script in a product review runs in a staff member's admin session
An injection flaw in the shop search passes through the orders API to the database

api_security.summary: The orders API checks the token but not who owns the order, so one customer reads others
Payment webhooks are accepted without a signature check, so anyone can mark orders paid

data_security.summary: Order exports with personal data sit in a bucket the deploy key can read
Bulk reads through the orders API pull customer records out of the database

devsecops_supply_chain.summary: A malicious pull request or a taken-over CI account exposes the deploy-prod key
A compromised CI pipeline deploys a modified shop container

incident_response.summary: Order exports are being downloaded from an unknown address with the deploy key
A web shell in the shop container keeps the attacker in after a password reset

grc_risk.summary: A breach through the shop web app reaches stored payment tokens
Personal data exports are kept indefinitely in a bucket nobody reviews

security_operations.summary: WAF blocks from one address are followed by a successful staff sign-in from it
The audit log shows the deploy key used from a residential address at night

reviewNotes: Beginner: one account, obvious paths (a leaked CI key, a public bucket, missing MFA, an API that trusts any valid token, unverified webhooks). Webhooks bypass the CDN, so the WAF does not apply to them.
